assessment.nobel_worthiness: A foundational account of how collateral constraints link financial conditions to aggregate fluctuations, with enduring influence on macroeconomic analysis.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki, Gertler and Moore are central architects of the core collateral and financial-accelerator mechanisms; the broader listed programme raises manageable boundary questions.
assessment.maturity: The mechanisms have been deeply incorporated into macro-finance theory and became especially salient in analysis of major credit disruptions.
uncertainties: The empirical size and universality of financial-accelerator effects remain model- and context-dependent.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection transformed modern trade theory and clarified the distributional and aggregate consequences of trade integration.
assessment.attribution: Melitz supplied the canonical heterogeneous-firm framework, while Helpman and Redding made major complementary theoretical contributions to the broader research programme.
assessment.maturity: The approach is mature, widely used in quantitative and empirical trade research, and has generated a durable body of evidence.
uncertainties: The contribution overlaps with several adjacent modern-trade literatures, making the precise prize boundary important.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Alternating-offer bargaining supplied an exceptionally influential, tractable framework for strategic bargaining and its application to markets.
assessment.attribution: Rubinstein is indispensable for the alternating-offers solution, and Wolinsky is a central contributor to bargaining-in-markets applications.
assessment.maturity: The ideas are longstanding, canonical, and broadly embedded in theory and applied economic modeling.
uncertainties: A prize formulation must distinguish the core bargaining breakthrough from the wider bargaining literature.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic-panel GMM methods materially expanded credible empirical work where fixed effects, persistence and endogeneity interact.
assessment.attribution: Arellano and Bond are identified with the original estimator, and Blundell and Bond with the influential system-GMM extension.
assessment.maturity: These methods are established workhorses across applied economics and their strengths and limitations are well understood.
uncertainties: Their widespread use has also exposed finite-sample and instrument-proliferation problems that limit mechanical application.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This work made political institutions, incentives and state capacity central analytical objects in understanding fiscal policy and development.
assessment.attribution: Besley, Persson and Tabellini each have distinct and major contributions to the modern political-economy programme.
assessment.maturity: The theoretical and empirical literatures are extensive and their questions remain central to comparative political economy.
uncertainties: The programme is broad, so a final citation would need a sharper unifying contribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic discrete-choice methods created a powerful bridge between dynamic economic theory and empirically estimable structural models.
assessment.attribution: Rust's breakthrough is foundational, with Keane and Eckstein making central extensions and applications in the named programme.
assessment.maturity: The methods have had sustained influence in labor, industrial organization and other fields over several decades.
uncertainties: The broad structural-methods tradition involves additional important contributors beyond the proposed laureates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The misallocation framework gave a disciplined quantitative language for relating distorted factor allocation to productivity and income gaps.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh, Restuccia and Klenow are leading contributors to the formulation and development of the named research agenda.
assessment.maturity: The framework has generated substantial follow-on theoretical, measurement and policy research.
uncertainties: Inference about distortions from observed dispersion is sensitive to modeling assumptions and measurement choices.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nominal rigidities and the New Keynesian framework fundamentally organized modern monetary-policy analysis and communication.
assessment.attribution: Calvo's pricing formulation and Woodford's and Gali's synthesizing theoretical contributions are central, though many additional scholars have strong claims.
assessment.maturity: The framework is exceptionally mature and remains a standard benchmark for central-bank and academic work.
uncertainties: The candidate grouping is unusually broad and exceeds the practical attribution capacity of a single prize.
